title: Hip Thrust
summary: Barbell hip thrust from a bench: glutes 1, hamstrings 0.4. Hardest at the top, where the glutes are shortest.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; flat bench.

muscles.why: The glute max extends the hip. With the shins vertical at the top, the glutes take most of it.

region_notes.text: Set-equated hip thrusts and back squats grew the glute max similarly in untrained adults.

muscles.why: The hamstrings help extend the hip but the bent knee limits them (0.4).
The glute medius helps keep the knees out: minor.
The quads hold the knee angle; below the counting floor (0.2).

setup.text: Upper back on a bench edge, just below the shoulder blades.
Bar padded across the hip crease.
Feet flat, about hip width; shins vertical at the top.

form_cues.why: Chin tucked, ribs down keeps the movement at the hips, not the lower back.

form_cues.cue: Drive the hips up until level with your torso
form_cues.why: Full hip extension at the top is where the glutes work hardest.
A one-second pause at the top stops you bouncing.

form_cues.cue: Tuck your chin and ribs down so your lower back doesn't arch at the top.
form_cues.why: Hip thrusts and squats grew the glutes similarly; squats also grew the quads and adductors.
Keeps the work on the hips, not the quads.

bias_tweaks.effect: More time where the glutes are hardest working.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back to finish instead of extending the hips.
mistakes.fix: Tuck the chin and ribs; lighten the load if the lower back arches.

mistakes.text: Arching the lower back at the top.
Feet too close so the quads take over.

misconceptions.myth: Hip thrusts are the best glute builder.
misconceptions.reality: They grew the glutes about the same as squats.

misconceptions.myth: Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: Ramp up before your first working set. For primary lifts the app suggests 50% x 8, 70% x 4 and 85% x 2 when the first working load is 60 kg or more, and 50% x 8 then 75% x 3 below that.
lower_risk.note: High-load warm-ups improved strength performance in a systematic review; the percentages are coaching convention.

lower_risk.text: Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 6-10 rep range. Stop the set when you can't reach full hip extension.
Pad the bar; set up with the bench secure so it can't slide.

alternatives.why: Similar glute growth plus quads and adductors.

notes: Hip-thrust findings are one study in untrained adults.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
